Normality Factor It is the numerical value by which the actual strength (in terms of normality) of a solution differs from expected sfrength. In the case, when exact weight of the substance seems to be difficult to weigh due to different reasons, then the weight of the substance slightly higher or lower than the required weight can be taken. In such a case, the normality factor should be introduced. The expected strength is multiplied by this factor to get the true strength.
Numerically, Weight taken (observed weight)
Normality factor = Weight to be taken (theoretical weight)

Titration Titration is the technique of deternzining the strength of unknown solution by reacting it with the standard solution by means of volume measurement normally in presence of third chenzical substance. For this, a known volume Of a solution is taken in a conical flask with the help of a pipette. Another solution is taken in a burette and these two soluüons are made to react with each other completely and, the end point of üfration is detected.

Volumetric Analysis End point of titration is the point of contpletion of reaction in titration which is shown by the colour change of third chemical substance i.e. indicator: In case of alkalimetery and acidimetry, it is also called as neutralization point.

Indicator is the third chemical substance used in titration which helps to predict the end point of titration by its colour change. In some cases, titrant (the solution in the burette) or titrand (the solution in the conical flask) ibelf acts as an indicator and is called self-indicator or auto-indicator.

Examples of indicator: Methyl orange, phenolphthalein Indicator Colour in acidic medium Colour in alkaline medium Methyl orange Light yellow Pink Phenolphthalein Pink Colourless Note: KMn04 solution; K2Cr207 solution etc. act as self-indicators.
Equivalence Point of Reaction NaCl + H20 HCl + NaOH NaS04 + 21-120 H2S04 + 2NaOH Any two substances always react in equal number of gram It is also called law of equivalents.
Equivalence point of reaction is a theoretical end point of the reaction.

At this point, n gram equivalent of a substance (say acid) reacb with n gram equivalent of another substance (say base). The difference between observed and theoretical end points is called titration error.
This error can be minimized by selecting a suitable indicator as far as possible.
